short_answer: Chris Jordan is a handicapper sold by Sports Advisors, Inc., a store with a roster of about a dozen names, among them Brandon Lang, Steve Budin (listed as CEO) and Al DeMarco (listed as GM). His page there has a full price list and a dated results feed, and the sister site DeMarco Sports runs his free picks. In that narrow sense the service is real and buyable.

Whether the picks win over time is a separate question. The page shows lines like "Winning Day # 45 of 74" and "$1 Bettors have made $44,630" without saying when the count starts or showing the full list. We found no independent record of his picks.

We also found almost no buyer talk about him at all: no reviews, no complaints, and one passing forum mention. Treat Chris Jordan as an unproven seller, and know that the store's terms say all sales are final.

guarantee: There is no performance guarantee. The sales terms say "All sales are final," that a terminated subscription gets no refund, and that pay per view picks are "not subject to any return policy." The FAQ adds that there is no guarantee "regarding the performance of a handicapper's selection."

The FAQ says some handicappers now and then sell a play they call "guaranteed," with terms shown at purchase. His page notes that any free service resulting from such a release is NOT included in his packages. A buyer who loses gets nothing back, and betting losses are never covered.

claims_note: Every record on the page is a run or a total that starts where the seller chose. "Winningest at this Site" compares him only with the other handicappers the same store sells.

The dollar figure assumes a $1 bet per unit, and his plays are rated in large unit sizes such as 600 and 800. Without the full list and the start date, a buyer cannot check how the $44,630 was reached or what a smaller bettor would have made.
The FAQ argues that long term buyers keep results honest because a lie would cost the store its customers. That is an argument, not an audit.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Chris Jordan pick with line, odds and release time, no third party tracking, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: a results feed with unit sizes. On 16 Nov 2026 the latest dated entry was "November 15: 800♦ Kansas City Chiefs" marked as a win, and DeMarco Sports showed a free 4 unit under in a Monday night NFL game. These are graded by the store that sells the picks.
The FAQ sends readers to the home page for "hot streaks, records, etc." and does not explain how plays are graded.

customers_intro: We found almost no independent customer evidence about Chris Jordan. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no buyer reviews, positive or negative, about Chris Jordan. The only independent mention we could open was a single TheRX forum post from 1 Nov 2026 that passed along one of his plays next to a Brandon Lang play, with no comment on his record. Two old Sportsbook Review threads carry his name but would not open, our Reddit archive check failed, and we found no complaints, refund disputes or praise anywhere else. With this little to go on, there is no pattern either way; the reader has only the seller's own numbers.

In TheRX thread that tracks Brandon Lang picks, one member noted that Brandon Lang and Chris Jordan "from Al's Website" were both on the Broncos +1.5. The reply was about the game, not about Chris Jordan. Al DeMarco is listed as GM of the Sports Advisors and DeMarco Sports sites, which may be the site meant, but the post does not say.

Our Reddit archive searches (Arctic Shift, r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting) timed out on 16 Nov 2026, so we could not check Reddit this time. Two Sportsbook Review threads titled "Chris Jordan" redirected or returned not found. Web searches found no Covers thread, review site entry, BBB record, news story or court record about him.

The FAQ says the store has no relationship with any sportsbook and that handicappers get no sportsbook kickbacks. We saw no sportsbook links on the pages we opened.
The same store sells Brandon Lang. See our Brandon Lang page for what bettors say about that service.

concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw comes from the store that sells the picks.

checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A run that starts on a chosen date is not a record.
Count units, not wins. Big unit plays that lose cost more than small ones that win.
Read the sales terms before paying. Here all sales are final.
Watch the free picks for a few weeks and write each one down with the line you could actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is sold by a real store, Sports Advisors, Inc., with published prices and written sales terms. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no full record is published, and we found no buyer reviews or complaints, and no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Chris Jordan cost?
On 16 Nov 2026 his Sports Advisors page listed a single pick or one day pass at $99, 7 plays at $199, 30 plays at $479, 30 days at $999 and 365 plays at $1,995.
Does Chris Jordan have a verified record?
No. The page shows runs such as "Winning Day # 45 of 74" and a $44,630 total for $1 bettors, all published by the seller with no full log or start date.

Nobody outside the seller has shown that his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110. All sales are final, so a losing package is simply lost. If you are curious, track his free picks yourself first.
